subject: On‑prem TLS/DNS handoff: auth-pathhook and cert responsibilities
messages:

Subject: On‑prem TLS/DNS options for private endpoints

Markus —

Thanks for taking this. We are finalizing the architecture for our private deployment of Redwood inside our VPC-connected on‑prem stack and need to lock down TLS + DNS responsibilities before the pilot. High level asks: 

- Can Redwood terminate TLS at an internal ingress (your sidecar/proxy) or do we need to own termination inside our perimeter?
- If Redwood terminates, how do we do private DNS delegation for acme.internal (split‑DNS)? Who creates zone/records and who rotates certs?
- We run an internal PKI (EAB/ACME compatible) and prefer to manage leaf cert issuance from our CA, but we need guidance on mutual TLS and client cert mapping for tenants.

Attached: mutual_tls_requirements.xlsx — includes our rotation policy and HSM requirements.

Preferred: a short call Thu morning to align on responsibilities and a two‑week plan to run a handoff.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Senior SRE — Acme Financial
ops-security@acme-corp.com

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com

Subject: Re: On‑prem TLS/DNS options for private endpoints

Hi Jane — great summary. Quick answers up front, then a proposed path: 

Options (pros/cons):
1) Redwood sidecar termination (recommended for fastest onboarding)
   - Pros: Redwood controls ingress TLS config, can enforce token-level routing and consistent telemetry; easier rollback.
   - Cons: Customer must delegate internal FQDNs via split resolver or provide internal DNS delegation; leaf certs can be customer‑issued (CSR exchange) or issued by Redwood if customer allows.

2) Customer‑owned termination (your proxy)
   - Pros: Customer full control over PKI and HSM; easier for strict compliance zones.
   - Cons: More ops for customer; requires us to provide exact SLA for protocol compatibility (ALPN, SNI mapping, gRPC/http/mtls nuances).

3) Hybrid: ACME sidecar + split resolver
   - Redwood runs a local ACME sidecar inside the runtime to request short‑lived leaf certs from your internal CA via EAB; Redwood still controls the proxy config, you own CA root and rotation.

Recommended path for Acme Financial pilot: Hybrid (3). Reasoning: keeps your root on‑prem (HSM), allows short‑rotation leaf certs, and reduces manual CSR exchange while letting Redwood manage runtime TLS settings. 

Immediate asks from Redwood to proceed: 
- Inventory of the FQDNs you want us to serve for pilot (fully qualified internal names).
- Confirmation you can expose an internal ACME endpoint or provide an EAB flow for short‑lived cert issuance.
- Desired rotation cadence (default we recommend 30–90 days for leaf certs).
- A contact for DNS/admins who can create the delegation/stub zone for our service discovery (or we will provide a small Terraform script you run).

I can run a 45‑minute workshop Thu 10:00–10:45 PDT to sketch the handoff and runbook. If that works, I’ll send an invite with an agenda: 1) DNS split strategy, 2) ACME/CSR options, 3) ingress proxy mapping, 4) rollback and audit.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com, mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2026-08-20T13:01:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: auth-pathhook approach and quick implementation notes

Team — looping you in with the Acme asks. Agreed recommendation is Hybrid (ACME sidecar) for pilot. A few internal constraints/ops notes to decide before the workshop: 

- Cert ownership: customer root in HSM. Redwood should accept either CSR upload (acme_csr.pem) or EAB ACME flow. For CSR uploads we need a small UI + SRE ticket flow; for ACME, we should support EAB keys in the sidecar.
- DNS: prefer stubzone/delegation to customer resolver; alternatively they run a tiny forwarder we provide (we must avoid public delegation).
- Rotation: support 90‑day by default, but set an API to accept requested TTL/validity per host. 
- Audit: each rotation must log UID, issuing method, and a signature proof stored in customer‑facing audit logs (push to their SIEM).
- Fallback: if ACME flow fails, we can accept a short‑lived CSR from customer and schedule a manual rotation window.

Karthik — can your infra team produce the sidecar image with EAB support and a flag to run in ‘customer‑managed‑root’ mode by end of next week?
Mina — please draft a one‑page runbook (DNS delegation steps + CSR exchange) and a short checklist for compliance (HSM + audit exports).

Thanks — I’ll bring this to the workshop.

- Markus

- We can expose an internal ACME broker endpoint (EAB) but need Redwood to authenticate with client cert + signed JWT (we’ll give a service identity).
- For DNS: we’ll create a stub zone for internal resolution and can apply the Terraform snippet if Redwood provides it.

We’re available Thu 10:00 PDT — I’ll accept the calendar invite.
